config.display.compactNumbers.descriptio: Show token counts in compact format using K/M suffixes (e.g. 1.5K, 1.2M). When disabled, full numbers are shown (e.g. 1,500, 1,200,000).

config.display.hideAutomaticToolCalls.de: In the Tool Usage view, hide tools marked "auto" (tools Copilot calls automatically, e.g. file reads and searches) so purposeful/intentional tool calls stand out. Disable to show automatic tool calls again.
config.display.statusBar.showTokens.desc: Controls which token counts are shown in the status bar. Token counts are estimated from session log files.
config.display.statusBar.showTokens.enum: Do not show token counts in the status bar
Show the last 30 days (rolling window) token count only
Show the current calendar month's token count only
Show both today's and last 30 days' token counts (default)
Show both today's and current calendar month's token counts
config.display.statusBar.showCost.descri: Controls which estimated costs (in USD) are shown in the status bar. Cost is estimated using GitHub Copilot AI-Credit rates (Usage Based Billing).
config.display.statusBar.showCost.enum.n: Do not show estimated cost in the status bar (default)
config.display.statusBar.showCost.enum.l: Show the last 30 days (rolling window) estimated cost only
config.display.statusBar.showCost.enum.c: Show the current calendar month's estimated cost only
config.display.statusBar.showCost.enum.b: Show both today's and last 30 days' estimated costs
config.display.statusBar.showCost.enum.t: Show both today's and current calendar month's estimated costs
config.display.statusBar.monthlyBudget.d: Monthly AI spend budget in USD. When set above 0, the status bar will change color as you approach the limit: yellow at 75%, orange at 90%, red at 100% or over. Set to 0 to disable budget coloring. Cost is estimated using GitHub Copilot AI-Credit rates.

usage.claudeDesktopCoverage.tooltip:
Claude Desktop lists every session it knows about, but this extension can only measure sessions whose transcript is still on this machine. Two things remove a transcript from local disk:

• Claude Code deletes transcripts older than its retention window (the cleanupPeriodDays setting, 30 days by default). Raise it in ~/.claude/settings.json to keep more history measurable.
• Sessions that ran in the cloud never write a transcript to this machine at all.

These sessions are not missing from your account — they are just not measurable locally.

insight.marathonSessionToday.title: 🧵 A very long chat session today
insight.marathonSessionToday.body: Your longest chat today{0} reached {1}{2}. Deep work in one chat is great — but once a session gets this long, earlier context is more likely to be summarized, compressed, or dropped, so replies can drift and slow down. When the goal changes, start a fresh chat (New Chat / `/new`) and paste a short handoff summary. A handy rule: one chat per bug, feature, or refactor.
insight.veryLongSessionsPattern.title: 📏 Your chats tend to run long
insight.veryLongSessionsPattern.body: Over the last 30 days your longest conversation reached {0} prompts, and your sessions average {1} prompts each. Very long chats make earlier context less reliable — the assistant may compress or ignore it as the window fills. Keeping one focused chat per task (and starting fresh when the topic shifts) usually produces sharper, faster answers.
insight.frequentManualCompaction.title: 🎉 You're managing context like a pro
insight.frequentManualCompaction.body: You've used `/compact` {0} times in the last 30 days — that shows deliberate context management, which is a real power-user habit. One refinement: `/compact` is best for continuing the *same task* when a chat gets long. When you're switching to a *new subtask*, a fresh chat (`/new`) with a short handoff summary usually produces sharper answers, since compaction already condenses earlier detail. Rule of thumb: `/compact` = same task, `/new` = new goal.
insight.autoCompactionPattern.title: ⚠️ Your sessions are auto-compacting frequently
insight.autoCompactionPattern.body.one: Your sessions automatically compacted {0} time in the last 7 days ({1}).{2} Auto-compaction means earlier context was lost without your control — you may have noticed replies suddenly lacking earlier detail. To avoid this: start a fresh chat (`/new`) when switching tasks, and use `/compact` yourself in Claude before the window fills.
insight.autoCompactionPattern.body.other: Your sessions automatically compacted {0} times in the last 7 days ({1}).{2} Auto-compaction means earlier context was lost without your control — you may have noticed replies suddenly lacking earlier detail. To avoid this: start a fresh chat (`/new`) when switching tasks, and use `/compact` yourself in Claude before the window fills.

Head it off by starting a fresh chat (`/new`) per task with a short handoff summary, running `/compact` yourself while you still control what's kept, and narrowing context to the files that matter instead of whole-repo references.

Reserve the heavier models for complex multi-step reasoning, architecture decisions, or subtle bugs.
